```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
options(width = 76)
# A figure whose pixels are all opaque is written without its alpha channel:
# the same pixels in a smaller file.
opaque_png <- function(path) {
  x <- png::readPNG(path)
  if (length(dim(x)) == 3 && dim(x)[3] == 4 && all(x[, , 4] == 1)) {
    png::writePNG(x[, , 1:3], path)
  }
  path
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 5.4, out.width = "100%", dpi = 117,
                      fig.process = if (requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE)) opaque_png)
```

This page starts from your own data: a depth raster, one or more lists of candidate stations,
and a range test. It lays the candidates side by side, scores them on the same simulated
animals, and writes the chosen stations for the field crew. The candidates can be arrays for a
new study or changes to an array already in the water, such as moving or adding stations. The
Stoney Lake example data of **arraydesign** and of the
[**detfield**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/) R package stand in for yours. Each
step is explained in [Get started](arraydesign.html).

```{r opening-coverage, echo = FALSE, purl = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.height = 5.6, fig.alt = "Three maps of Stoney Lake in magma colours with yellow receiver rings: the 20 planned stations on a grid, 20 at random, and a grid of 30, each with bright patches round the receivers and most of the water dark."}
# Run the code of sections 1, 3 and 4 to draw Figure 1 first; the code is
# shown there
opening_chunks <- c("read-your-files", "your-own-range-model",
                    "deployable-water", "lay-out-planned-array",
                    "lay-out-other-arrays", "build-detection-fields",
                    "array-coverage", "map-candidate-coverage")
opened <- eval(parse(text = unlist(knitr::knit_code$get(opening_chunks))))

# Give the share of water at p >= 0.5 under a design, in percent
share_at_half <- function(design) {
  round(100 * mean(array_cover$p[array_cover$design == panel_names[[design]]] >= 0.5))
}
coverage_map
```

*Figure 1. Probability that at least one receiver of each candidate array hears one
transmission from each 100 m water cell of Stoney Lake, under the range model fitted in
section 2: (a) the 20 planned stations; (b) 20 receivers at random; (c) a grid of 30.*

With ten more receivers, the grid of 30 brings `r share_at_half("grid_30")`% of the water to a
probability of 0.5 or more; the planned 20 reach `r share_at_half("planned")`% and 20 at random
`r share_at_half("random_20")`%. Section 5 scores what the extra receivers
add to detections and positions.

`system.file("scripts", package = "arraydesign")` holds this page's code as `design-an-array.R`;
copy it and change the file names to yours.

## 1. Read your files

The depth raster is in a projected coordinate system in metres, with land as `NA`; depth may be
stored as positive or negative numbers. The station list has a `station_id` and either
`deploy_lat` and `deploy_lon` in WGS 84 or `x` and `y` in the raster's coordinate system. The
range test has one row per receiver, tag and hour, with the receiver's depth, the distance to
the tag, the transmissions sent and the detections heard. Here the range test is
`detfield::stoney_range_test`, two lines of receivers at 1 m and 25 m simulated from the
example's assumed range model; read yours with `read.csv()`. Replace the paths with yours.

```{r read-your-files}
# Load the package, and ggplot2 for the figures
library(arraydesign)
library(ggplot2)

# Read your depth raster and candidate stations
lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "arraydesign"))
planned <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "planned_stations.csv",
                                package = "arraydesign"))

# Take the range test: one row per receiver, tag and hour
range_test <- detfield::stoney_range_test

# Check the raster's coordinate system and cell size, m
terra::crs(lake, describe = TRUE)$code
terra::res(lake)

# Check the stations, and the receiver depths of the range test, m
head(planned, 3)
table(range_test$depth_m)
```

## 2. The range model: yours or the default

You fit the range model to your own range test, with
the model of your choice, and pass the fit to `detfield::de_model()`. Here it is a logistic
regression on distance, receiver depth and their interaction.

```{r your-own-range-model}
# Fit a logistic regression of detections on distance and receiver depth
range_fit <- glm(cbind(heard, sent - heard) ~ distance_m * depth_m,
                 family = binomial, data = range_test)

# Pass the fit to detfield as the range model of this page
range_model <- detfield::de_model(range_fit)
range_model
```

A model that also varies over time, by hour or season, goes in through `detfield::de_model()`
the same way; the
[**detfield** range-model article](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/range-model.html)
fits one.

`detfield::de_logistic()` stands in where no range test was run: a logistic curve through
`d50` and `d05` given at two receiver depths and interpolated between them. [Get started](arraydesign.html) uses it with the
example's assumed values. The chunk reads both models at the two depths of the test and at
10 m, between them.

```{r compare-the-two-models}
# Set the stand-in of Get started: d50 and d05 for receivers 1 m and 35 m deep
stand_in <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),
                                  depth = c(1, 35))

# Read the detection probability of each model at 250, 500 and 750 m
distances <- c(250, 500, 750)
probability <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 10, 25), function(depth) {
  data.frame(depth_m = depth, distance_m = distances,
             fitted = round(plogis(range_model$predict(distances,
                                                       depth_m = depth)), 3),
             stand_in = round(plogis(stand_in$predict(distances,
                                                      depth_m = depth)), 3))
}))
probability
```

The next chunk finds the largest difference between the two at each depth, over every 10 m
from 0 to 1,500 m.

```{r largest-difference}
# Find the largest difference in detection probability, and where, per depth
fine_distances <- seq(0, 1500, by = 10)
largest <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 10, 25), function(depth) {
  gap <- abs(plogis(range_model$predict(fine_distances, depth_m = depth)) -
               plogis(stand_in$predict(fine_distances, depth_m = depth)))
  data.frame(depth_m = depth, largest = round(max(gap), 3),
             at_m = fine_distances[which.max(gap)])
}))
largest
```

The two agree at 1 m and 25 m, where the test has data, and differ at 10 m: a test at two
depths cannot say how range changes between them. Receivers deeper than 25 m are an
extrapolation. This page uses the fit.

## 3. Lay out the candidate arrays

Water shallower than 1 m is set to `NA` first, so that no grid or random receiver goes where it
cannot be moored.

```{r deployable-water}
# Set water shallower than 1 m to NA
deployable <- terra::ifel(abs(lake) < 1, NA, lake)
```

Your station list goes in with `method = "manual"`; the stations keep their names, and
`deploy_z` is the depth under each. The station file included with the package holds the 20-receiver grid of
Get started, so "planned" below is that array read from a file.

```{r lay-out-planned-array}
# Place the planned stations on the raster
planned_receivers <- place_receivers(lake, method = "manual",
                                     coords = planned)
head(planned_receivers, 3)
```

A station far onto land or off the raster is refused, and the message names its row. Here the
longitude of S003 has a typing slip:

```{r station-off-the-raster}
# Copy the planned stations with a slip in the longitude of row 3
stations_with_slip <- planned
stations_with_slip$deploy_lon[3] <- -78.29706

# Try to place them; place_receivers() refuses the row and names it
try(place_receivers(lake, method = "manual", coords = stations_with_slip))
```

The other candidates here are 20 receivers at random cells at least 1 km apart and a grid of
30. A second station list of your own goes in the same way as the first. `designs` holds the
three.

```{r lay-out-other-arrays}
# Name the three candidate arrays
designs <- list(
  planned = planned_receivers,
  random_20 = place_receivers(deployable, n = 20, method = "random",
                              spacing = 1000, seed = 1),
  grid_30 = place_receivers(deployable, n = 30, method = "grid", seed = 1)
)

# Count the receivers in each
sapply(designs, nrow)
```

The chunk gives the deepest receiver of each design, in metres.

```{r deepest-receivers}
# Give the depth of the deepest receiver in each design, m
round(sapply(designs, function(layout) max(layout$deploy_z)), 1)
```

The random layout and the grid of 30 each have a receiver deeper than 25 m, beyond the range
test.

A grid can also be set by its spacing; the number of receivers then follows from the water.

```{r grid-by-spacing}
# Count the receivers in a grid 2 km apart
nrow(place_receivers(deployable, spacing = 2000))
```

## 4. Map what each candidate hears

One detection field per design, built as in
[step 2 of Get started](arraydesign.html#build-the-detection-field-and-map-coverage).

```{r build-detection-fields}
# Build one detection field per design
fields <- lapply(designs, function(layout) {
  detfield::de_field(detfield::water_distances(lake, layout), range_model)
})
```

`coverage_summary()` gives single-receiver coverage of each design at 0.5 and 0.8.

```{r coverage-table}
# Count the coverage of each design, one row per design and threshold
coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fields), function(design) {
  cbind(design = design, coverage_summary(fields[[design]]))
}))
coverage
```

The chunk below stacks the array-level probability of
[step 2 of Get started](arraydesign.html#build-the-detection-field-and-map-coverage) for the
three designs, with the panel each is drawn in.

```{r array-coverage}
# Name the panels, in the order of `designs`
panel_names <- c(planned = "(a) planned, 20", random_20 = "(b) 20 at random",
                 grid_30 = "(c) grid of 30")

# Compute the probability that any receiver hears, per design and cell
array_cover <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fields), function(design) {
  data.frame(design = panel_names[[design]],
             p = 1 - apply(1 - fields[[design]]$p, 1, prod),
             terra::xyFromCell(lake, fields[[design]]$cells))
}))

# Give the share of water cells at p >= 0.5, per design
tapply(array_cover$p >= 0.5, array_cover$design, mean)
```

The next chunk draws Figure 1, at the top of the page.

```{r map-candidate-coverage, fig.show = "hide"}
# Stack the receivers of the designs, with the panel each is drawn in
design_rings <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(designs), function(design) {
  data.frame(x = designs[[design]]$x, y = designs[[design]]$y,
             design = panel_names[[design]])
}))

# Draw one panel per design: the array's probability, and the receivers on
# top as a dark ring under a coloured one, keyed by the shape scale
ring <- detfield::positionr_ring_colours()
coverage_map <- ggplot(array_cover, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = p)) +
  detfield::scale_fill_probability(name = "Detection\nprobability") +
  geom_point(data = design_rings, aes(shape = "Receiver"),
             colour = ring[["edge"]], size = 0.9, stroke = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = design_rings, aes(shape = "Receiver"),
             colour = ring[["heard"]], size = 0.9, stroke = 0.35) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Receiver = 21)) +
  facet_wrap(~design, ncol = 2) +
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
  detfield::annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +
  detfield::theme_positionr() +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.75, 0.25))
coverage_map
```

`listening` scores the coverage of the receivers in the water on a given day, such as one when
two have been pulled for download:

```{r coverage-while-two-receivers-are-out}
# Count the coverage of the planned array with S006 and S016 pulled
pulled <- c("S006", "S016")
coverage_summary(fields$planned,
                 listening = setdiff(planned_receivers$station_id, pulled))
```

## 5. Score the candidates on the same animals

`evaluate_array()` simulates animals, detects their transmissions through the field, positions
them and scores the positions, as in
[step 4 of Get started](arraydesign.html#simulate-animals-and-their-detections). The three
designs are scored on the same 20 animals over 6 hours: the same tracks and transmissions, heard
through each design's field.

```{r score-the-designs, message = FALSE}
# Evaluate each design on the same 20 animals, 6 hours each
evaluations <- lapply(designs, function(layout) {
  evaluate_array(layout, lake, range_model, n_animals = 20,
                 seed = 1, control = list(hours = 6, tag_delay = c(120, 180)))
})
```

The chunk returns the detection rate of every animal under every design.

```{r rate-per-animal}
# Tabulate the detection rate, one row per design and animal
rates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(evaluations), function(design) {
  sent <- evaluations[[design]]$detections$transmissions
  rate <- tapply(sent$n_detections > 0, sent$path_id, mean)
  data.frame(design = panel_names[[design]], animal_id = names(rate),
             rate = as.vector(rate))
}))
head(rates, 3)
```

The table puts coverage, detection and positioning side by side: `covered_p50`, the share of
water at 0.5 or more under one receiver alone; `mean_rate`, the mean detection rate per animal;
`scored_share`, the share of animal-hours with a detection, the only hours that can be
positioned; and `median_error_m`, the median error of the scored hours.

```{r compare-the-designs}
# Tabulate coverage, detection and positioning, one row per design
scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(evaluations), function(design) {
  overall <- evaluations[[design]]$score$overall
  design_rates <- rates$rate[rates$design == panel_names[[design]]]
  data.frame(design = design, receivers = nrow(designs[[design]]),
             covered_p50 = round(evaluations[[design]]$coverage$share[1], 3),
             mean_rate = round(mean(design_rates), 3),
             never_heard = sum(design_rates == 0),
             scored_share = round(overall$scored_share, 3),
             median_error_m = round(overall$median_error_mean_m))
}))
scores
```

Figure 2 shows where the differences in `mean_rate` come from: each animal under each array.

```{r plot-rate-by-design, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Detection rate of each of 20 simulated animals under three candidate arrays, with a grey line joining each animal across the arrays, a bar at the mean, and the number of animals never heard written under each array."}
# Compute the mean rate, and the animals never heard, per design
rate_means <- aggregate(rate ~ design, data = rates, FUN = mean)
never <- aggregate(rate ~ design, data = rates,
                   FUN = function(rate) sum(rate == 0))
never$label <- sprintf("%d at 0%%", never$rate)

# Draw each animal across the designs, its points joined, the means, and
# the count of animals never heard, which overlap at 0
ggplot(rates, aes(design, rate)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = animal_id), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(colour = "#21908C", alpha = 0.8, size = 1.8) +
  geom_errorbar(data = rate_means, aes(ymin = rate, ymax = rate), width = 0.4,
                colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = never, aes(y = -0.07, label = label), size = 3.2,
            colour = "grey20") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(share) sprintf("%g%%", 100 * share),
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), limits = c(-0.1, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Candidate array", y = "Share of transmissions heard") +
  detfield::theme_positionr()
```

*Figure 2. Detection rate of each of 20 simulated animals across 6 hours under the three
candidate arrays of Figure 1; lines join one animal across the arrays, and bars mark the
mean across animals. Animals never heard overlap at 0%, so the label under each array counts
those overlapping points. The animals, their tracks and their transmissions are the same under
all three.*

The grid of 30, with ten more receivers, scores `r round(100 * scores$scored_share[3], 1)`% of
animal-hours against `r round(100 * scores$scored_share[1], 1)`% for the planned 20, with a
median error of `r scores$median_error_m[3]` m against `r scores$median_error_m[1]` m. Read the
error beside the scored share: an array that hears few animal-hours can still report a small
error for the few it hears. Twenty animals over six hours are a small sample, and a difference
of a few percent can come from which animals were drawn; raise `n_animals` and `hours` before you
choose.

The planned array is the grid of Get started read from a file. The next chunk scores the grid as
Get started lays it, and the planned array under both models, on the same animals.

```{r planned-under-both-models}
# Score the grid of Get started and the planned array under the stand-in
reference_settings <- list(hours = 6, tag_delay = c(120, 180))
grid_stand_in <- evaluate_array(
  place_receivers(deployable, n = 20, method = "grid", seed = 1), lake,
  stand_in, n_animals = 20, seed = 1, control = reference_settings
)
planned_stand_in <- evaluate_array(designs$planned, lake, stand_in, n_animals = 20,
                                   seed = 1, control = reference_settings)

# Compare the hit rates, with the planned array under the fitted model
round(c(grid_stand_in = grid_stand_in$score$overall$hit_rate,
        planned_stand_in = planned_stand_in$score$overall$hit_rate,
        planned_fitted = evaluations$planned$score$overall$hit_rate), 3)
```

The next chunk compares the two hour by hour: the detections each array heard, and the
animal-hours whose share of true positions inside the 95% region differs.

```{r station-file-against-grid}
# Compare the station file and the grid, detections and each animal-hour
same_detections <- identical(planned_stand_in$detections$detections,
                             grid_stand_in$detections$detections)
by_hour <- merge(planned_stand_in$score$bins, grid_stand_in$score$bins,
                 by = c("animal_id", "bin_start"), suffixes = c("_file", "_grid"))
differs <- by_hour[by_hour$in_region_file != by_hour$in_region_grid,
                   c("animal_id", "bin_start", "in_region_file", "in_region_grid")]
same_detections
differs
```

Under the stand-in the planned array scores
`r sprintf("%.3f", planned_stand_in$score$overall$hit_rate)` and the grid
`r sprintf("%.3f", grid_stand_in$score$overall$hit_rate)` (the hit rate: the mean share of an
hour's true positions inside its 95% region). The two differ because the station file gives
the grid in latitude and longitude, and the conversion from degrees shifts each receiver by a
few millimetres. Under the
fitted model the planned array scores `r sprintf("%.3f", evaluations$planned$score$overall$hit_rate)`.

### Positioning with a shorter range

A range test describes one place, one season and one transmitter. `perturb_de_model()` copies
the range model with a shorter range, here half, and `evaluate_array()` positions with that copy
while the animals are still detected under the true curve.

```{r position-with-half-the-range, message = FALSE}
# Halve d50 and d05 of the range model
half_range_model <- perturb_de_model(range_model, d50_scale = 0.5,
                                     d05_scale = 0.5)

# Detect under the true curve; position with the halved one
half_range_eval <- evaluate_array(
  designs$planned, lake, range_model, n_animals = 20, seed = 1,
  control = list(hours = 6, tag_delay = c(120, 180),
                 position_model = half_range_model)
)
```

The table compares the error and hit rate of the two.

```{r compare-the-ranges}
# Compare the median error and the hit rate, true range against half
score_columns <- c("median_error_mean_m", "hit_rate")
rbind(true_range = evaluations$planned$score$overall[score_columns],
      half_range = half_range_eval$score$overall[score_columns])
```

Positioned with half the true range, the planned array's median error is
`r round(half_range_eval$score$overall$median_error_mean_m)` m, against
`r round(evaluations$planned$score$overall$median_error_mean_m)` m. Its hit rate falls to
`r sprintf("%.3f", half_range_eval$score$overall$hit_rate)` from
`r sprintf("%.3f", evaluations$planned$score$overall$hit_rate)`.

## 6. Write the stations for the field crew

Once a design is chosen, write its stations with their coordinates and the depth at each. Here
the file goes to a temporary folder; give your own path.

```{r write-the-chosen-stations}
# Keep station, position and depth of the chosen design, depth to 0.1 m
chosen <- designs$planned
field_sheet <- chosen[c("station_id", "deploy_lat", "deploy_lon", "deploy_z")]
field_sheet$deploy_z <- round(field_sheet$deploy_z, 1)

# Write the sheet and read it back
sheet_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "stations_for_deployment.csv")
write.csv(field_sheet, sheet_file, row.names = FALSE)
head(read.csv(sheet_file), 3)

# Count the stations under 2 m deep
sum(chosen$deploy_z < 2)
```

Check with the crew that a receiver can be moored at the
`r sum(chosen$deploy_z < 2)` stations under 2 m deep before the sheet goes out. After
deployment, the detections and the deployment log go to the
[**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/) R package, which reads, checks and filters
them, and then to **detfield**, which positions the animals with the range model you used here.

## Point and click

The [**arraydesignR**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesignR/) R package is
**arraydesign** as a point-and-click application. It reads a depth raster and a station CSV,
places receivers by grid, from the CSV or by clicking on the map, maps coverage, walks
simulated animals and gives their detection rates, and writes the stations as a CSV. Its range
model is `d50` and `d05` entered at two receiver depths; a fitted range model and positioning
stay in code. Install it with `remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/arraydesignR")` and start it with
`arraydesignR::run_app()`.
